indication_label: biallelic RPE65-mediated inherited retinal disease (ICER candidate population, no viable-cell restriction)
verbatim: The US population represents approximately 50.06% of the total population in the US and the five major European markets (Germany, France, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom). Applying that proportion to the total of 3,500 patients results in an estimate of approximately 1,750 eligible individuals in the US.
source_doc: ICER, Voretigene Neparvovec for Biallelic RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 14 Feb 2018, section 4.3 Potential Budget Impact
notes: ICER budget-impact candidate population = all US individuals with biallelic RPE65 IRD, derived from Spark's 10-K figure of 3,500 in US+EU5; no adjustment for 'sufficient viable retinal cells'. Text extracted from the PDF locally.

indication_label: biallelic RPE65-mediated IRD (ICER five-year spread of the prevalent pool)
verbatim: Assuming equal distribution over five years, this resulted in an estimate of 350 patients eligible for VN in the US per year.
source_doc: ICER, Voretigene Neparvovec for Biallelic RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 14 Feb 2018, section 4.3 Potential Budget Impact
notes: Budget-impact convention (1,750 / 5), not an incidence estimate. ICER: 'the relatively small number of patients assumed to be treated per year (350)'. Actual US treated numbers (75 vials in 2018) were far below this.

indication_label: persons in the US with RPE65-mediated IRDs (manufacturer preliminary estimate as cited by ICER)
verbatim: Preliminary estimates from the manufacturer suggest that there are between 1,000 and 3,000 persons in the US with RPE65-mediated IRDs.
source_doc: ICER, Voretigene Neparvovec for Biallelic RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 14 Feb 2018, section 1 Background
notes: ICER citing Spark (its reference 9). Wider than Spark's own 1,000-2,000 (3 Jan 2018 release, already in luxturna_disclosures.csv). Not restricted to viable retinal cells.

indication_label: individuals with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal diseases
geography: US and EU5 (Germany, France, Italy, Spain, UK)
verbatim: we used inputs from a US Securities and Exchange Commission Form 10-K Annual Report by Spark Therapeutics, Inc., which estimated "that there are approximately 3,500 individuals with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal diseases in the United States and the five major European markets."
source_doc: ICER, Voretigene Neparvovec for Biallelic RPE65-Mediated Retinal Disease: Effectiveness and Value, Final Evidence Report, 14 Feb 2018, section 4.3, quoting Spark Therapeutics Form 10-K
notes: Spark 10-K figure as quoted by ICER. By ICER's 50.06% population split this implies about 1,750 in the EU5 as well as 1,750 in the US.

indication_label: LCA or RP with biallelic RPE65 mutations, GKV-insured (before viable-cell restriction)
verbatim: Die Zahlen basieren auf Praevalenzdaten von Patienten mit Leberscher kongenitaler Amaurose (LCA) und Retinitis pigmentosa (RP), jeweils mit biallelischen RPE65-Mutationen; es ergibt sich unter Beruecksichtigung der niedrigsten und hoechsten Praevalenz eine Spanne aus dem minimalen und maximalen Anteil von 188 bis 655 Patienten (im Mittel 355 Patienten).
source_doc: G-BA, Tragende Gruende zum Beschluss ueber die Nutzenbewertung von Voretigen Neparvovec (Luxturna), 17 Oct 2019, section 2.2
notes: Manufacturer (Novartis) dossier figures adopted by G-BA; mean 355. GKV covers about 88% of the German population. Umlauts transliterated in verbatim.

indication_label: label population incl. 'ausreichend lebensfaehige Netzhautzellen', GKV-insured
verbatim: In einem naechsten Schritt findet der minimale und maximale Anteil behandelbarer Patienten Beruecksichtigung; die resultierende Patientenpopulation von ca. 100 bis 530 Patienten ergibt sich aus dem zugelassenen Anwendungsgebiet, das auf diejenigen Patienten mit "ausreichend lebensfaehigen Netzhautzellen" einschraenkt. Die Berechnung des Umfangs der Zielpopulation liegt in der Gesamtschau in einer plausiblen Groessenordnung, ist jedoch mit Unsicherheiten behaftet.
source_doc: G-BA, Tragende Gruende zum Beschluss ueber die Nutzenbewertung von Voretigen Neparvovec (Luxturna), 17 Oct 2019, section 2.2
notes: Official G-BA eligible count for Germany (statutory insurance). Prevalent pool at EU launch; G-BA calls the order of magnitude plausible but uncertain.

indication_label: label population incl. sufficient viable retinal cells, GKV-insured (2019 figures retained)
verbatim: Den Angaben werden die Daten des pharmazeutischen Unternehmers aus dem Dossier der Erstbewertung von Voretigen Neparvovec aus dem Jahr 2019 zugrunde gelegt. [...] die resultierende Patientenpopulation von ca. 100 bis 530 Patientinnen und Patienten ergibt sich aus dem zugelassenen Anwendungsgebiet, das auf diejenigen Patientinnen und Patienten mit "ausreichend lebensfaehigen Netzhautzellen" einschraenkt.
source_doc: G-BA, Tragende Gruende zum Beschluss (Neubewertung nach Fristablauf) Voretigen Neparvovec, 15 Sep 2022, section 2.2
notes: Re-assessment after the time limit. G-BA explicitly preferred the 2019 numbers over the newer figures in the 2022 dossier, which it judged more uncertain. No separate incident-flow figure given.

indication_label: adult and paediatric patients with vision loss due to IRD caused by confirmed biallelic RPE65 mutations with sufficient viable retinal cells (public drug plans)
unit: patients eligible, year 1 of sponsor budget-impact analysis
verbatim: Number of patients eligible for the drug under review: 43 / 25 / 18
source_doc: CADTH Pharmacoeconomic Report: Voretigene Neparvovec (Luxturna), appendix 'Submitted Budget Impact Analysis and CADTH Appraisal', January 2021 (NCBI Bookshelf NBK569020)
notes: Sponsor BIA years 1-3 = 43, 25, 18. Assumptions: prevalence of RP 0.025%; proportion of RP due to RPE65 mutation 1.404%; incidence of RP 0.0006%; prevalence of LCA 0.003%; proportion of LCA due to RPE65 6.80%; proportion of diagnosed patients with sufficient viable retinal cells 60%. Year 1 includes the prevalent backlog. CADTH reanalysis changed diagnosis rates but did not publish a parallel eligible-count table.

indication_label: as above
unit: patients eligible, year 2 of sponsor BIA
verbatim: Number of patients eligible for the drug under review: 43 / 25 / 18
source_doc: CADTH Pharmacoeconomic Report: Voretigene Neparvovec (Luxturna), appendix 'Submitted Budget Impact Analysis and CADTH Appraisal', January 2021 (NCBI Bookshelf NBK569020)
notes: Year 2 of the sponsor's three-year budget impact analysis.

indication_label: as above
unit: patients eligible, year 3 of sponsor BIA
verbatim: Number of patients eligible for the drug under review: 43 / 25 / 18
source_doc: CADTH Pharmacoeconomic Report: Voretigene Neparvovec (Luxturna), appendix 'Submitted Budget Impact Analysis and CADTH Appraisal', January 2021 (NCBI Bookshelf NBK569020)
notes: Year 3; approximates the steady-state annual flow (incident plus late-diagnosed) once the backlog is worked through.

indication_label: people eligible for voretigene neparvovec in England (company estimate accepted in NICE HST11)
verbatim: [search-result summary] The company estimated that 86 people would be eligible for treatment with voretigene neparvovec in England.
source_doc: NICE HST11, final evaluation determination / committee papers (search-result summary)
notes: nice.org.uk returned HTTP 403 for the FED document and for the guidance PDF; web.archive.org is blocked for this tool, so the sentence was not read in the source. Same figure as the provisional row in luxturna_disclosures.csv, but this cites the FED document.

indication_label: population cible (HAS avis de la Commission de la Transparence)
source_doc: HAS, avis de la Commission de la Transparence LUXTURNA (voretigene neparvovec), 2019
notes: has-sante.fr aborted the connection on four attempts (fr, en and pprd pages); archive.org blocked. The avis contains a 'population cible' paragraph that still needs to be read manually.

indication_label: estimated patients per year (MSAC application 1623 public summary document)
source_doc: MSAC Public Summary Document, application 1623, voretigene neparvovec (Luxturna), 2020
notes: msac.gov.au timed out on both the legacy (1623-public) and current URL. Luxturna was funded in Australia via MSAC/NHRA rather than PBAC, so the PSD is the gatekeeper document to read.

indication_label: adults with idiopathic macular telangiectasia type 2 (US label)
verbatim: ENCELTO is an allogeneic encapsulated cell-based gene therapy indicated for the treatment of adults with idiopathic macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel).
source_doc: Neurotech Pharmaceuticals press release with Highlights of Prescribing Information, 'Neurotech's ENCELTO Approved by the FDA for the Treatment of Macular Telangiectasia Type 2', 6 Mar 2025
notes: Adults only; one implant per affected eye (disease is usually bilateral), so implants per patient can approach 2. The press release gives no prevalence or patient-number statement. US availability from June 2025. Not approved outside the US as of Sep 2026.

indication_label: MacTel type 2 detected on fundus photographs, adults aged 43-86
verbatim: a prevalence of 0.1% in the age group analyzed
source_doc: Charbel Issa P et al., Macular telangiectasia type 2, Prog Retin Eye Res 2013 (PMC3638089), section on prevalence, citing Klein R et al., The prevalence of macular telangiectasia type 2 in the Beaver Dam Eye Study, Am J Ophthalmol 2010
notes: Population base: 4,790 Beaver Dam Eye Study participants aged 43-86 at baseline (1988-90), regraded from stereoscopic fundus photographs; PubMed abstract (20609708, cookie-walled) gives 95% CI 0.09-0.1. Highest published estimate; the review says photo-based grading likely underestimates true prevalence.

indication_label: MacTel type 2 on non-mydriatic macular images, mean age 65
verbatim: a lower prevalence, estimated to range from 0.004 to 0.022%
source_doc: Charbel Issa P et al., Macular telangiectasia type 2, Prog Retin Eye Res 2013 (PMC3638089), section on prevalence, citing Aung KZ et al., Melbourne Collaborative Cohort Study, 2010
notes: Just over 22,000 participants; images were graded for MacTel only if an earlier grading flagged a feature, so probably an undercount. Kenya/Nigeria population studies (Sallo 2012) gave 0.06% (combined 95% CI 0.02-0.14%).

indication_label: MacTel type 2, all adults (0.1% prevalence applied to the US population)
verbatim: MacTel type 2 impacts around 0.1% of the population, translating to approximately 165,000 patients in the United States.
source_doc: Claritas Rx blog, 'A Breakthrough in Vision Care: The FDA Approval of Neurotech's Encelto', 2025 (citing Endpoints News, endpts.com/fda-approves-neurotech-therapy-for-rare-eye-disease/)
notes: Trade-press arithmetic, not a Neurotech statement; blog undated (approval date used). 0.1% of the whole US population would be about 335,000, so 165,000 implies 0.1% applied to roughly the population over 40. Upper-bound prevalent pool; most are undiagnosed and many have late disease beyond the trial population.

indication_label: MacTel type 2, US population aged 45 and over, published prevalence range
source_doc: Derived here from Beaver Dam (0.1%) and Melbourne (0.004%) rates x US population aged 45+ (about 139 million: 2020 Census, ages 45-64 plus 65+)
notes: 0.004% x 139m = 5,560; 0.1% x 139m = 139,000. Neither rate is diagnosis-based; the diagnosed, adult, idiopathic pool eligible under the label is far smaller and undocumented.

indication_label: severe-to-profound/profound SNHL with biallelic OTOF variants, preserved outer hair cell function, no prior cochlear implant in the same ear (US label)
verbatim: For the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound and profound sensorineural hearing loss (HL; any frequency >90 dB) associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic variants in the OTOF gene, preserved outer hair cell function, and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear.
source_doc: FDA, OTARMENI (lunsotogene parvec-cwha) product page, STN 125874, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, approval 23 Apr 2026
notes: Accelerated approval. The no-prior-implant and preserved-OHC criteria exclude most prevalent OTOF-deaf people (already implanted or with degraded OHC function), so the eligible pool is essentially the annual flow of newly diagnosed infants plus a small backlog of unimplanted ears. Regeneron provides the product free in the US, so treated patients will not appear in revenue. No ex-US approval.

indication_label: newborns per year with OTOF-related hearing loss
verbatim: estimated to affect approximately 50 newborns annually in the United States
source_doc: CGTLive, 'Regeneron Nets Accelerated Approval From FDA for Otoferlin-Related Hearing Loss Gene Therapy Lunsotogene Parvec', 24 Apr 2026 (reporting Regeneron's figure)
notes: Secondary report of the company estimate; Regeneron's own release (investor.regeneron.com and newsroom mirror) timed out on three attempts. CHORD pivotal cohort: 20 participants aged 10 months to 16 years.

indication_label: newborns per year with otoferlin-related hearing loss
verbatim: [search-result summary] Otoferlin-related hearing loss is ultra-rare, affecting 20-50 newborns per year in the U.S.
source_doc: Regeneron DB-OTO press releases 2023-2025 as summarised in search results (e.g. 'DB-OTO Results in the New England Journal of Medicine...')
notes: Company phrasing used before approval; the exact release was not confirmed because investor.regeneron.com timed out. Consistent with the 50/year figure quoted at approval. as_of_date approximate.

indication_label: people in the US with otoferlin-related deafness, all ages (mostly implanted, so NOT label-eligible)
verbatim: [search-result summary] otoferlin-related deafness occurs in about 10-20,000 people in the U.S.
source_doc: Search-result summary attributing the figure to 'one researcher'; candidate page MedCity News, 'Regeneron Gets Landmark FDA Approval for First Gene Therapy for Hearing Loss', Apr 2026
notes: Attribution unverified. Upper bound on the unimplanted backlog only: the label excludes ears with a prior cochlear implant and most prevalent cases are implanted.

indication_label: adult and paediatric patients 8 years and older with GSDIa, adjunct to nutritional management (US label)
verbatim: GENGLYCOS (pariglasgene brecaparvovec-opnr) is indicated to reduce daily cornstarch intake as an adjunct to nutritional management in adult and pediatric patients 8 years of age and older with glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSDIa).
source_doc: Ultragenyx press release, 'Ultragenyx Announces U.S. FDA Approval of GENGLYCOS Gene Therapy...', 19 Aug 2026 (GlobeNewswire)
notes: Accelerated approval; label age floor 8 years. The post-marketing study excludes patients with anti-AAV8 antibodies and secondary reporting (Yahoo Finance) describes the label as for patients 'who do not have antibodies to AAV8'; confirm in the PI. Pivotal GlucoGene study treated 46 participants aged 8+. No ex-US approval.

indication_label: patients with GSDIa, all ages (company estimate)
verbatim: GSDIa affects 1,500-2,500 patients in the U.S. and 6,000-8,000 worldwide within commercially accessible geographies.
source_doc: Ultragenyx press release, 19 Aug 2026 (GlobeNewswire)
notes: Company estimate, all ages; not restricted to age 8+ or AAV8-seronegative. The statement appears twice in the release.

indication_label: patients with GSDIa, all ages (company estimate)
verbatim: GSDIa affects 1,500-2,500 patients in the U.S. and 6,000-8,000 worldwide within commercially accessible geographies.
source_doc: Ultragenyx press release, 19 Aug 2026 (GlobeNewswire)
notes: Ex-US commercially accessible pool by subtraction: 3,500-6,500 (6,000-8,000 minus 1,500-2,500).

indication_label: glycogen storage disease type I (Ia = 80%)
verbatim: The incidence of GSD I in the overall population is 1 in 100,000 live births, with GSD Ia being more common (80%) than GSD 1b (20%).
source_doc: Nana M, Anastasopoulou C, Parikh NS, Ahlawat R, Glycogen Storage Disease Type I, StatPearls (NCBI Bookshelf NBK534196), last update 6 Apr 2025
notes: Population base: live births. GSDIa share 80% gives 0.8 per 100,000 births. Same 1-in-100,000 figure is used in Ultragenyx-funded literature (Ultragenyx page and PMC11716495 were blocked: 403 / reCAPTCHA). Ashkenazi Jewish prevalence about 5x.

indication_label: GSDIa births per year (become label-eligible at age 8)
source_doc: Derived here: 3.6 million US live births per year (CDC 2023: about 3.59m) x 1/100,000 x 0.8 (GSDIa share, StatPearls)
notes: 3,600,000 / 100,000 x 0.8 = 28.8. The annual flow into label eligibility is the birth cohort reaching age 8 (about 30/yr), assuming full survival. Company prevalent estimate (1,500-2,500) implies a mean prevalence of roughly 0.5-0.75 per 100,000, consistent with this incidence.

indication_label: adults with genetically confirmed familial LPLD, severe or multiple pancreatitis attacks despite low-fat diet, detectable LPL protein (EU label)
verbatim: Alipogentiparvovec ist zugelassen fuer erwachsene Personen, bei denen eine familiaere LPLD diagnostiziert wurde und bei denen schwere oder multiple Pankreatitis-Schuebe trotz fettarmer Ernaehrung aufgetreten sind. Die Diagnose LPLD muss durch einen Gentest abgesichert sein. Die Anwendung ist beschraenkt auf Patienten mit nachweisbaren Mengen an LPL-Protein.
source_doc: G-BA, Nutzenbewertung (Dossierbewertung fuer Orphan Drugs) Alipogentiparvovec, 2 Feb 2015, section 2.1
notes: EU approval Oct 2012 (exceptional circumstances); marketing authorisation not renewed, expired Oct 2017. Adults only, with the pancreatitis restriction, so the label pool is a fraction of all LPLD. Search snippet (G-BA press coverage): only one person received Glybera commercially by 2016.

indication_label: adult patients with familial LPLD and severe or multiple pancreatitis attacks despite dietary fat restriction (EU label, EPAR wording)
verbatim: Glybera is indicated for adult patients diagnosed with familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency (LPLD) and suffering from severe or multiple pancreatitis attacks despite dietary fat restrictions.
source_doc: EMA, Glybera EPAR medicine page (alipogene tiparvovec), authorised 25 Oct 2012, marketing authorisation expired 28 Oct 2017
notes: EPAR page carries no prevalence statement (the CHMP assessment report cited by G-BA gives about 2 per million in the EU). Authorisation expired 28 Oct 2017 after uniQure chose not to seek renewal, so the exposure window is Oct 2012 to Oct 2017.

indication_label: familial lipoprotein lipase deficiency, all patients
verbatim: Die Praevalenz der LPLD liegt in der EU bei etwa 2 pro 1 Million Personen (CHMP, 2012).
source_doc: G-BA, Nutzenbewertung Alipogentiparvovec, 2 Feb 2015, section 2.1, citing the CHMP assessment report 2012
notes: Population base: total EU population. All LPLD, not the label subset.

indication_label: people with lipoprotein lipase deficiency, all (orphan designation)
verbatim: lipoprotein lipase deficiency affected approximately 0.02 in 10,000 people in the European Union (EU). This was equivalent to a total of around 930 people
source_doc: EMA, orphan designation EU/3/04/194, alipogene tiparvovec for treatment of lipoprotein-lipase deficiency, 9 Mar 2004 (sponsor later uniQure biopharma B.V.)
notes: 0.02 per 10,000 = 2 per million on an EU population of about 465m (2004). Upper bound for the label pool; the adult, severe/recurrent-pancreatitis, detectable-LPL subset was never quantified by a gatekeeper in the documents retrieved.

indication_label: LPL deficiency, all patients
verbatim: [search-result summary] LPL Deficiency affects 1-2 persons per million
source_doc: NORD, 'Glybera Becomes First-ever Gene Therapy Approved in Europe' (and similar 2012 coverage) as summarised in search results
notes: Snippet only; the exact page carrying this sentence was not fetched. Matches the CHMP 2 per million figure.

indication_label: people with LPLD, all (2 per million applied to Germany)
source_doc: Derived here: CHMP/G-BA prevalence 2 per million x German population 83,118,501 (Destatis 2022, as cited in IQWiG G25-25)
notes: 166 all-LPLD; GKV share 88.6% gives about 147. Label subset (adults with severe/multiple pancreatitis and detectable LPL protein) unknown; the G-BA 2015 Beschluss count was not retrieved.

indication_label: people with LPLD, all (2 per million applied to France)
source_doc: Derived here: 2 per million x French population about 68.1 million (INSEE 2023)
notes: All LPLD; HAS population cible not retrieved (site unreachable).

indication_label: Anzahl der Patienten in der GKV-Zielpopulation (G-BA Beschluss 21 May 2015)
source_doc: G-BA Beschluss and Tragende Gruende, Alipogentiparvovec, 21 May 2015 (procedure page)
notes: The 2015 Beschluss/TrG with the patient count was not retrieved; the 2017 TrG (deadline extension, 18 May 2017) and the 2015 G-BA Nutzenbewertung contain no count. Modul 3 (24 Oct 2014, g-ba.de/downloads/92-975-701/...) would carry the manufacturer's derivation.

indication_label: population cible (HAS avis)
source_doc: HAS, avis de la Commission de la Transparence GLYBERA (alipogene tiparvovec), 2015
notes: has-sante.fr aborted the connection twice; archive.org blocked.

indication_label: LPLD prevalence or eligible patients (company filing)
source_doc: uniQure N.V. Form 10-K for FY2016 (filed 15 Mar 2017)
notes: No prevalence or eligible-patient figure for LPLD in the FY2016 10-K (Glybera already being wound down). Earlier uniQure filings (20-F FY2013/FY2014, 10-K FY2015) not checked; search budget exhausted.

indication_label: wound treatment from birth in DEB with mutation(s) in COL7A1 (EU label)
verbatim: Demnach ist Beremagen geperpavec zur Wundbehandlung bei Patientinnen und Patienten ab der Geburt mit dystropher Epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) mit Mutation(en) im Gen fuer die Alpha-1-Kette von Kollagen Typ VII (COL7A1) zugelassen [1].
source_doc: IQWiG Dossierbewertung G25-25, Beremagen geperpavec (dystrophe Epidermolysis bullosa), Bewertung von Patientenzahlen und Therapiekosten, Version 1.0, 6 Nov 2025, section 3.1
notes: EU label (EC approval Apr 2025) from birth; both dominant and recessive DEB. US label at launch (May 2023) was 6 months and older; Krystal announced an updated FDA label in 2025 (not verified here). Weekly topical gel, so the eligible population is the prevalent DEB pool with wounds, treated continuously.

indication_label: patients with wounds due to DEB with COL7A1 mutation, GKV-insured
verbatim: Patientinnen und Patienten mit Wunden aufgrund dystropher Epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) mit Mutation im Gen fuer die Alpha-1-Kette von Kollagen Typ VII (COL7A1) circa 240 - 900 Patientinnen und Patienten
source_doc: G-BA Beschluss ueber die Nutzenbewertung von Beremagen geperpavec (Vyjuvek), 19 Feb 2026 (BAnz AT 23.03.2026 B3), section 2
notes: Official G-BA count (Beschluss section 2). Tragende Gruende (same date): figures taken from the manufacturer dossier, uncertain because of limited German incidence/prevalence data, but 'in einer weitgehend plausiblen Groessenordnung'. GKV = 88.6% of population.

indication_label: dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, all (prevalence range used in the German dossier)
verbatim: Der pU leitet auf der Basis dieser beiden Publikationen somit eine Spanne der Praevalenzrate von 3,26/1 000 000 Personen [2] bis 12,16/1 000 000 Personen [3] ab.
source_doc: IQWiG Dossierbewertung G25-25, Beremagen geperpavec (dystrophe Epidermolysis bullosa), Bewertung von Patientenzahlen und Therapiekosten, Version 1.0, 6 Nov 2025, section 3.1
notes: Lower bound = Fine 2016 (US National EB Registry, 2002 data); upper bound = Has et al. 2023 (1,779 German EB patients identified via university hospitals, labs and DEBRA Deutschland, Oct 2020-May 2021; the authors treat their estimate as an upper bound). IQWiG: plausible order of magnitude.

indication_label: dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, all patients in Germany
verbatim: Durch Multiplikation mit der in Schritt 1 abgeleiteten Spanne der Praevalenzrate berechnet der pU eine Anzahl von 271 bis 1011 Patientinnen und Patienten mit dystropher Epidermolysis bullosa in Deutschland im Jahr 2022.
source_doc: IQWiG Dossierbewertung G25-25, Beremagen geperpavec (dystrophe Epidermolysis bullosa), Bewertung von Patientenzahlen und Therapiekosten, Version 1.0, 6 Nov 2025, section 3.1
notes: Whole-population count (83,118,501) before the GKV share; manufacturer (Krystal) derivation accepted by IQWiG as plausible.

indication_label: DEB with COL7A1 mutation and wounds, GKV-insured (manufacturer dossier)
verbatim: Unter Beruecksichtigung eines GKV-Anteils von 88,6 % [4,5] im Jahr 2022 weist der pU eine Anzahl von 240 bis 896 Patientinnen und Patienten in der GKV-Zielpopulation aus.
source_doc: IQWiG Dossierbewertung G25-25, Beremagen geperpavec (dystrophe Epidermolysis bullosa), Bewertung von Patientenzahlen und Therapiekosten, Version 1.0, 6 Nov 2025, section 3.1
notes: Manufacturer figure reviewed by IQWiG; G-BA rounded to 240-900 in the Beschluss. Projection: 244-910 in 2023 and 246-917 in 2030 (constant prevalence, Destatis population projection).

indication_label: DEB with COL7A1 mutation and wounds, GKV-insured (projection)
verbatim: Der pU geht somit davon aus, dass die Anzahl der Patientinnen und Patienten mit dystropher Epidermolysis bullosa sowie der gesetzlich Versicherten innerhalb der Zielpopulation (bei Anwendung der Anteilswerte aus der Herleitung) bis zum Jahr 2030 weitgehend konstant bleibt (Fallzahlen in der GKV-Zielpopulation: 244 bis 910 im Jahr 2023 und 246 bis 917 im Jahr 2030).
source_doc: IQWiG Dossierbewertung G25-25, Beremagen geperpavec (dystrophe Epidermolysis bullosa), Bewertung von Patientenzahlen und Therapiekosten, Version 1.0, 6 Nov 2025, section 3.1
notes: Genetic disease, so incidence and prevalence assumed constant; 2030 projection 246-917.

indication_label: dystrophic AND junctional EB, age 6 months+, GKV-insured (Filsuvez decision 2022; comparator count)
verbatim: Im Rahmen des frueheren Nutzenbewertungsverfahrens zu Birkenrindenextrakt (Epidermolysis bullosa) aus dem Jahr 2022 [6-8] wurde eine Anzahl von ca. 270 bis 860 Patientinnen und Patienten in der GKV-Zielpopulation beschlossen.
source_doc: IQWiG Dossierbewertung G25-25, Beremagen geperpavec (dystrophe Epidermolysis bullosa), Bewertung von Patientenzahlen und Therapiekosten, Version 1.0, 6 Nov 2025, section 3.1
notes: G-BA count for Filsuvez (birch bark extract), which covers DEB plus junctional EB from 6 months; upper bound there came from Petrof 2022 (England and Wales). Useful cross-check: DEB-only range for Vyjuvek is similar because the German upper-bound source (Has 2023) is higher.

indication_label: population cible, wounds in DEB with COL7A1 mutation(s) from birth (HAS avis, manufacturer estimate)
verbatim: [search-result summary] The industriel estimates the target population at 522 patients per year.
source_doc: HAS, avis de la Commission de la Transparence, VYJUVEK (beremagene geperpavec), epidermolyse bulleuse dystrophique des la naissance, Nov 2025 (page p_3704146)
notes: has-sante.fr aborted on three attempts (fr and en pages; OMEDIT mirror carries only the indication) and the CEESP avis economique (p_3894631) was not fetched. Date approximated from HAS's tweet announcing the favourable opinion (6 Nov 2025). An earlier avis for the 6-months-and-older indication (p_3543140, 2024) and an early-access authorisation also exist. For a weekly gel 'per year' is effectively the prevalent treated pool.

indication_label: eligible patients in England (NICE technology appraisal ID3959, in development)
source_doc: NICE, Beremagene geperpavec for treating skin wounds associated with dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa [ID3959], GID-TA10868, project information
notes: Appraisal still in development (TSOP Sept 2023 kept it in the TA programme); no NICE eligible count published. Search snippet from stakeholder comments: most DDEB patients have low wound burden, so 'only small numbers (likely <10%)' of DDEB would meet a wound-area threshold.

indication_label: all epidermolysis bullosa (any type), UK; DEB stated as 25% of EB
unit: people with EB (all types, not DEB-only)
verbatim: One in 227 people carry a defective gene that causes EB. One in 17,000 live births will be a baby with EB and around 5,000 people in the UK live with EB.19 25% of the EB population have DEB.14
source_doc: NIHR Innovation Observatory, Health Technology Briefing: Beremagene geperpavec for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, April 2021
notes: All EB types; NIHR cites DEBRA UK. Derived DEB pool below. Document contains no B-VEC-specific eligible count.

indication_label: dystrophic EB, UK (25% of 5,000 EB patients)
source_doc: Derived here from NIHR Innovation Observatory 2021: 5,000 people with EB in the UK x 25% DEB
notes: 5,000 x 0.25 = 1,250. Higher than the registry-based England and Wales figure (about 640) because the DEBRA 5,000 is a round advocacy estimate.

indication_label: dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, living registered patients
verbatim: By March 2021, 2594 individuals were registered, of whom 2361 were living, which yielded a prevalence of 34.8 per million of the population for all EB types [EB simplex (EBS) 17 per million, dystrophic EB (DEB) 10.7 per million, junctional EB (JEB) 1 per million and Kindler EB 0.3 per million].
source_doc: Petrof G, Papanikolaou M, Martinez AE et al., The epidemiology of epidermolysis bullosa in England and Wales: data from the national epidermolysis bullosa database, Br J Dermatol 2022;186(5):843-848 (abstract via KCL Pure)
notes: National EB database covering all four EB centres (high ascertainment). Population base: England and Wales, about 59.6 million (2021 census). Used by G-BA as the upper bound in the 2022 Filsuvez decision.

indication_label: dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, incidence
verbatim: The average incidence per million live births for EBS, DEB, JEB and Kindler EB was 32.5, 26.1, 8.9 and 0.9, respectively (total incidence for all types of EB was 67.8 per million).
source_doc: Petrof G, Papanikolaou M, Martinez AE et al., The epidemiology of epidermolysis bullosa in England and Wales: data from the national epidermolysis bullosa database, Br J Dermatol 2022;186(5):843-848 (abstract via KCL Pure)
notes: Population base: live births in England and Wales (about 625,000 per year in 2021).

indication_label: dystrophic EB, living patients (registry rate applied to population)
source_doc: Derived here: Petrof 2022 DEB prevalence 10.7 per million x England and Wales population 59,597,300 (2021 census)
notes: 10.7 x 59.6 = 638 (England alone, 56.5m: about 604). Registry-based, so a lower bound on all DEB but close to the diagnosed pool relevant to a prescribed weekly therapy. Compare Krystal's 'over 1,000 identified' in Germany plus France.

indication_label: dystrophic EB births per year
source_doc: Derived here: 26.1 per million live births x 624,828 live births (ONS, England and Wales 2021)
notes: 26.1 x 0.625 = 16.3 per year; EU label from birth makes these immediately eligible.

indication_label: dominant dystrophic EB, all subtypes
unit: per 1,000,000 population (incidence 2.12 per million live births)
verbatim: DDEB (all subtypes): Prevalence of 1.49 per million population; incidence of 2.12 per million live births
source_doc: Fine JD, Epidemiology of Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa Based on Incidence and Prevalence Estimates From the National Epidermolysis Bullosa Registry, JAMA Dermatology 2016;152(11):1231-1238
notes: US National EB Registry, prevalence as of 2002, incidence 1986-2002 (16 years). Abstract wording as extracted by the fetch tool. Overall inherited EB: incidence 19.57 per million live births, prevalence 11.07 per million.

indication_label: recessive dystrophic EB, all subtypes
unit: per 1,000,000 population (incidence 3.05 per million live births)
verbatim: RDEB (all subtypes): Prevalence of 1.35 per million population; incidence of 3.05 per million live births
source_doc: Fine JD, Epidemiology of Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa Based on Incidence and Prevalence Estimates From the National Epidermolysis Bullosa Registry, JAMA Dermatology 2016;152(11):1231-1238
notes: Search snippet adds DEB of unknown mode 0.42 per million (not in the abstract text fetched).

indication_label: dystrophic EB (DDEB + RDEB), registry rates applied to US population
source_doc: Derived here: (1.49 + 1.35) per million x US population about 335 million (Census 2023)
notes: 2.84 x 335 = 951 (about 1,090 if DEB of unknown mode 0.42 per million is added). Registry-based lower bound; Krystal's claims-based estimate is over 3,000, i.e. the registry captured roughly a third.

indication_label: dystrophic EB births per year, registry rates
source_doc: Derived here: (2.12 + 3.05) per million live births x 3.6 million US births (CDC 2023)

Company figure; value_point is the stated floor.

indication_label: DEB patients worldwide (company estimate)

indication_label: DEB patients in the United States (company estimate, repeated)
verbatim: We believe that there are, at present, over 3,000 DEB patients in the United States and over 9,000 worldwide.
source_doc: Krystal Biotech Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 17 Feb 2026), Business section
notes: Unchanged from FY2024. The 10-K gives no Japan-specific figure.

indication_label: DEB patients identified in Germany and France (first EU launch markets)
verbatim: Over 1,000 DEB patients are already identified across both of these countries.
source_doc: Krystal Biotech Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 17 Feb 2026), Business section
notes: Identified, not on therapy. Consistent with G-BA 240-900 (GKV Germany, so about 270-1,010 whole population) plus HAS 522 per year (France).

source_doc: Krystal Biotech Form 10-K (FY2018 or adjacent year) as summarised in search results

indication_label: diagnosed prevalent DEB cases, seven major markets (US, EU4, UK, Japan)
geography: 7MM (US, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, UK, Japan)

notes: Market-research estimate; implies about 3,250 in the US and about 3,250 across EU4+UK+Japan. as_of_date approximate.

indication_label: DEB patients in Japan
source_doc: Krystal Biotech Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 17 Feb 2026), Business section
notes: No Japan figure in Krystal's FY2024 or FY2025 10-K; Japanese approval/launch materials and a PMDA figure were not reachable after the search budget ran out. DelveInsight 7MM figure above is the only source that spans Japan.

indication_label: wounds in adult and paediatric patients with RDEB (US label)
verbatim: indicated for the treatment of wounds in adult and pediatric patients with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (RDEB)
source_doc: Abeona Therapeutics press release, 'U.S. FDA Approves ZEVASKYN (prademagene zamikeracel)...', 29 Apr 2025 (approval 28 Apr 2025)
notes: Autologous gene-corrected keratinocyte sheets applied surgically in one session; no age floor. Press release has no prevalence statement. FY2025 10-K: first commercial patient treated Q4 2025; four qualified treatment centres activated as of March 2026. Not approved outside the US.

indication_label: recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, incidence (literature range)
verbatim: Similar to other rare diseases, the incidence and prevalence of RDEB are not well defined. Incidence of 0.2 to 3.05 per million births and prevalence of 0.14 to 1.35 per million people have been observed across different geographies, primarily estimated by limited population analyses of clinical databases or registries (Eichstadt et al.; Clinical, Cosmetic and Investigational Dermatology, 2019).
source_doc: Abeona Therapeutics Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 17 Mar 2026), Business section, RDEB disease overview
notes: Company summary of registry literature; upper bound equals Fine 2016 (US).

indication_label: recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, prevalence (literature range)
verbatim: Incidence of 0.2 to 3.05 per million births and prevalence of 0.14 to 1.35 per million people have been observed across different geographies, primarily estimated by limited population analyses of clinical databases or registries (Eichstadt et al.; Clinical, Cosmetic and Investigational Dermatology, 2019).
source_doc: Abeona Therapeutics Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 17 Mar 2026), Business section, RDEB disease overview
notes: Applied to 335m, the range gives 47-452 RDEB patients in the US.

indication_label: RDEB patients in the US whose wounds may benefit from COL7A1-mediated treatment (genetic-modelling upper bound)
verbatim: Using genetic modeling of COL7A1 variants, Stanford University estimated the incidence of RDEB to be approximately 63 per million births, and prevalence could be up to 3,850 patients in the U.S., whose wounds may benefit from COL7A1-mediated treatments such as ZEVASKYN.
source_doc: Abeona Therapeutics Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 17 Mar 2026), Business section, RDEB disease overview
notes: Carrier-frequency model, not observed cases; 63 per million births is about 20x the registry incidence, so this is an upper bound including undiagnosed and mild cases.

indication_label: moderate to severe RDEB patients in the US eligible for ZEVASKYN (claims analysis)
verbatim: Based on claims analysis, we estimate that approximately 750 moderate to severe RDEB patients in the U.S. would be ZEVASKYN eligible patients (Clearview Claims Analysis, 2024).
source_doc: Abeona Therapeutics Form 10-K for FY2025 (filed 17 Mar 2026), Business section, RDEB disease overview
notes: Company's central eligible estimate (diagnosed, moderate-to-severe, with wounds). Same 10-K: about 60% of RDEB patients have active wounds covering more than 30% of body surface (Bruckner 2020).

indication_label: recessive dystrophic EB, all subtypes (US registry)
unit: per 1,000,000 population (incidence 3.05 per million live births)
verbatim: RDEB (all subtypes): Prevalence of 1.35 per million population; incidence of 3.05 per million live births
source_doc: Fine JD, Epidemiology of Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa Based on Incidence and Prevalence Estimates From the National Epidermolysis Bullosa Registry, JAMA Dermatology 2016;152(11):1231-1238

indication_label: RDEB generalized severe (the subtype with the heaviest wound burden)
unit: per 1,000,000 population (incidence 0.57 per million live births)
verbatim: RDEB generalized severe: Prevalence of 0.36 per million population; incidence of 0.57 per million live births
source_doc: Fine JD, Epidemiology of Inherited Epidermolysis Bullosa Based on Incidence and Prevalence Estimates From the National Epidermolysis Bullosa Registry, JAMA Dermatology 2016;152(11):1231-1238
notes: Applied to 335m: about 121 prevalent RDEB-GS patients in the US; about 2 births per year.

indication_label: RDEB, all subtypes, registry rate applied to US population
source_doc: Derived here: Fine 2016 RDEB prevalence 1.35 per million x US population about 335 million
notes: 1.35 x 335 = 452. Registry-based lower bound; Abeona's claims-based eligible pool (750) and genetic-model ceiling (3,850) bracket it from above.

indication_label: RDEB births per year, registry rate
source_doc: Derived here: Fine 2016 RDEB incidence 3.05 per million live births x 3.6 million US births
notes: 3.05 x 3.6 = 11.0 per year; Stanford genetic model (63 per million) would give about 227 per year.
